Mixed results1-3 were obtained when ambroxol was used in chronic bronchitis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD—p.1112); in a randomised study, it was no better than placebo in preventing acute exacerbations of COPD; however, in a subset of patients with more severe dis- ease, ambroxol therapy reduced the number of exacerbations.4 It was ineffective5 when given to mothers for the prophylaxis of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (p.1508), although it may be of modest benefit in the early treatment of established disease in infants.6,7 Inhalation of ambroxol aerosol has also produced beneficial ef- fects in a patient with alveolar proteinosis who refused alveolar lavage.8 For the use of mucolytics in productive cough see p.1547. 1.
